articleTitle: Denoising of single-look SAR images based on variance stabilization and nonlocal filters
publicationTitle: 2010 International Conference on Mathematical Methods in Electromagnetic Theory
abstract: Synthetic-aperture radar (SAR) imaging has become an efficient tool for obtaining and retrieving useful information about surfaces of Earth and other planets. However, the formed images suffer from speckle noise, especially if single-look observation mode is used. Then, filtering is often applied to improve image quality and provide better estimation of radar cross-section and other parameters of sensed scenes. Recently, a novel class of image filters has proved to be very successful in the removal of additive white Gaussian noise from natural images; these filters are based on nonlocal image modeling, i.e. they exploit the mutual self-similarity of image patches at different locations in the image. These filters have been shown in several benchmarks to significantly outperform all previous techniques. In this paper, we evaluate the performance of nonlocal filters applied to the denoising of single-look SAR images corrupted by speckle with a Rayleigh distribution, taking advantage of exact forward and inverse variance-stabilizing transformations. Numerical simulations demonstrate the success of this approach against several known despeckling methods.

articleTitle: Statistical estimation of polarimetric method potential for dangerous turbulence detection in rain
publicationTitle: 2010 International Conference on Mathematical Methods in Electromagnetic Theory
abstract: In this paper the polarimetric approach for wind phenomena detection and study is proposed and analyzed. The polarimetric estimation of turbulence intensity is made with single unipolarized antenna radar system. The statistical estimation of proposed method is made.

articleTitle: Determining sources in the array of electric dipoles
publicationTitle: 2010 International Conference on Mathematical Methods in Electromagnetic Theory
abstract: Approach to source determining in the array of electric dipoles is suggested. This approach is based on non-linear regularization technique by using a functional of "generalized extension" of solution. Model of sources is described by a set of ideal Hertzian dipoles. The problem of non-linear optimization is formulated and algorithm based on conjugate gradient method is built. Results of computing simulation for one-dimension case when dipoles are located along line which is parallel to measurement line of electrical field are presented.

articleTitle: Analysis of transient fields reflected from model of huma body surface using convolutional neural network
publicationTitle: 2010 International Conference on Mathematical Methods in Electromagnetic Theory
abstract: The application of the operation of convolution based on artificial neural network processing for the problem of determination of thickness of layered medium layer by impulse irradiation is considered. The impulse fields reflected from the model of human body surface are analyzed by convolutional neural network in time domain directly. The normal incidence of plane wave with Gaussian time form on the layered medium with losses is considered. The reflected electromagnetic field is obtained by FDTD method. Initial data for the neural network analysis are the values of amplitude of electrical component of reflected field in different time points. As an example, the network is trained to determine the thickness of one of the layers of the medium. The stability of the determination is investigated by numerical simulation in presence of interferences, experimental errors and instabilities of medium parameters. The comparison between the determination by two-layered neural network and convolutional neural network is given.

articleTitle: Statistical study of multimodal tweek-atmospherics
publicationTitle: 2010 International Conference on Mathematical Methods in Electromagnetic Theory
abstract: A new technique is used for statistical analysis of experimental records of tweek-atmospherics (tweeks). Tweeks are observed during nighttime and represent response of the Earth-ionosphere waveguide to excitation by lightning strokes. TWEEKS are formed by series of pulses consecutively reflected from the waveguide boundaries under different incident angles depending on a source-observer distance and effective ionosphere height along a propagation path. The tweek signals demonstrate the propagation of a few Earth-ionosphere waveguide modes. We determined propagation path's parameters such as source range, ionosphere height, and azimuthal orientation of a propagation path. We used then a time-frequency representation of analyzed tweek waveforms to infer separate branches, corresponding to different waveguide modes. Obtained results show the increase of attenuation for higher modes with increase of a source distance.

articleTitle: Solution of the general differential maxwell system in vector form
publicationTitle: 2010 International Conference on Mathematical Methods in Electromagnetic Theory
abstract: The general differential Maxwell system is solved. Its investigation in vector form is done in the case of arbitrary disturbed anisotropic medium. The final solution is in conformity with other preceding results of this system study.

articleTitle: Power series for waves in micro-resonator arrays
publicationTitle: 2010 International Conference on Mathematical Methods in Electromagnetic Theory
abstract: We obtain convergent power-series representations for Bloch waves and their complex dispersion relation in an infinite periodic array of micro-resonators, which exhibits artificial bulk magnetism. The small parameter η of expansion is the ratio of period to wavelength, and the high conductivity is inversely proportional to η. The coefficient fields are solutions to an infinite sequence of period-cell problems.

articleTitle: Eigen modes of a square waveguide with two inner diagonally-placed square ridges
publicationTitle: 2010 International Conference on Mathematical Methods in Electromagnetic Theory
abstract: The analysis of E- and H- modes of a square waveguide with two inner diagonally-placed square ridges has been carried out on the base of the mode-matching numerical model. The relation between the field structures of modes of the considered and square waveguides has been established. Possible applications of such a waveguide have been discussed.

articleTitle: Spectral-domain approach to electromagnetic scattering from imperfectly periodic structures
publicationTitle: 2010 International Conference on Mathematical Methods in Electromagnetic Theory
abstract: A spectral-domain approach to the electromagnetic scattering from imperfectly periodic structures is shown based on the pseudo-periodic Fourier transform. The fields in imperfectly periodic structures have continuous spectra in the wavenumber space, and the main problem of the spectral-domain approach is the discretization scheme on the wavenumber. The present approach introduces the pseudo-periodic Fourier transform, which makes us possible to apply the conventional grating theory to the problems of imperfectly periodic structures.

articleTitle: Scattering of LSM modes in an E-plane two-port waveguide junction with triangular connecting cavity
publicationTitle: 2010 International Conference on Mathematical Methods in Electromagnetic Theory
abstract: In terms of LSM modes, the S-matrix of a waveguide two-port with triangular connecting cavity is found. The one is intended for the use in the analysis of piecewise homogeneous E-plane structures as a constituent part of the generalized scattering matrix of a triangular cell located between two interfaces.

articleTitle: Kinetic equation for electron in polar crystal in the presence of strong electric field
publicationTitle: 2010 International Conference on Mathematical Methods in Electromagnetic Theory
abstract: In the Bogolyubov method of reduced description of nonequilibrium states kinetic equation for electron in polar crystal has been obtained in the presence of homogeneous steady strong electric field without assumption about its weakness. A case of weak electron-phonon interaction is studied in detail.

articleTitle: Numerical results for the differential phase shift in the circular waveguide with azimuthally magnetized ferrite
publicationTitle: 2010 International Conference on Mathematical Methods in Electromagnetic Theory
abstract: Employing an iterative approach, an exact computation of the differential phase shift, provided by the circular waveguide, entirely filled with azimuthally magnetized ferrite, is performed in normalized form for the normal TE<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">01</inf> mode. The results obtained correspond to the upper part (consisting of two separate areas) relevant to small and large values of the off-diagonal ferrite permeability tensor element, of the frequency band in which the structure exhibits phase shifting properties. They complement previous ones for the lower part of the same. The joint consideration of the new and earlier outcomes shows that the phase shift increases almost linearly with the tensor element (is almost proportional to the reciprocal of normalized guide radius) in the whole band, if the radius (the tensor element) is fixed.

articleTitle: Using apriory information about analytic properties of the solution on mathematical modeling in wave diffraction and propagation theory
publicationTitle: 2010 International Conference on Mathematical Methods in Electromagnetic Theory
abstract: Wave diffraction mathematical modeling methods, using a priori information on analytical properties of the wave field, are reviewed.

articleTitle: Interpolation-type numerical method for electromagnetic wave diffraction by a perfectly conducting axially symmetric screen
publicationTitle: 2010 International Conference on Mathematical Methods in Electromagnetic Theory
abstract: A problem of monochromatic electromagnetic wave diffraction by a perfectly electrically conducting (PEC) surface of rotation located in an infinite homogeneous isotropic medium is investigated. The problem is reduced to sets of hypersingular and singular integral equations which is solved by the method of discrete singularities, using interpolation type quadrature formulas. From the solutions of these sets the scattered electric field expression and the scattering patterns is obtained.

articleTitle: Using conformal shape, separate and dynamical apodization to improve characteristics of multibeam active phased array
publicationTitle: 2010 International Conference on Mathematical Methods in Electromagnetic Theory
abstract: Some results of the project "Torus" are discussed. This paper is focused on 2 mutually complementary methods of improving characteristics of multibeam active phased arrays. Applications of these methods for ground based antennas, HATP and communication satellites are considered. Described methods can be also used for radars.

articleTitle: Method of approximation functions for solution of 2D nonlinear volterra integral equation
publicationTitle: 2010 International Conference on Mathematical Methods in Electromagnetic Theory
abstract: The approximation functions method for solution of an integral equation is considered. A nonlinear 2D Volterra integral equation which describes electromagnetic wave propagation in a nonlinear layer is solved by this method. Original software for computer modeling of such an algorithm is developed and numerical results are presented.

articleTitle: Vector boundary Riemann problems in soliton theory
publicationTitle: 2010 International Conference on Mathematical Methods in Electromagnetic Theory
abstract: Vector boundary homogeneous Riemann problem with specific matrix coefficient is solved explicitly in the framework of investigation of Landau-Lifshitz equation's general case. The given research, though is completely mathematical is in conformity with preceding physical approach of this equation study.

articleTitle: Some features of the null field method and method of auxiliary sources
publicationTitle: 2010 International Conference on Mathematical Methods in Electromagnetic Theory
abstract: Using the problem of cylindrical wave scattering by a perfectly conducting circular cylinder, it is shown that the conditions of the theorem concerning resolvability of the integral equation arising in the method of auxiliary sources are not necessary in the similar theorem formulated recently for resolvability of the integral equation arising in the null field method.

articleTitle: Dielectric-air structure as a component of electromechanically controlled microwave devices
publicationTitle: 2010 International Conference on Mathematical Methods in Electromagnetic Theory
abstract: Dielectric-air structure located between ideal metal plates is analyzed. It is shown that efficient mechanical alteration of propagation constant in this structure could be achieved only for those modes with non-zero component of electrical field perpendicular to border between dielectric and air. Scattering problem for the structure was reduced by partial domain method to set of 1-rst type Fredholm integral equations for the unknown tangential components of electric and magnetic fields at the boundaries of partial domains. The set of integral equations was solved by method of moments.

articleTitle: Meridian estimator performance for samples of generalized Gaussian distribution
publicationTitle: 2010 International Conference on Mathematical Methods in Electromagnetic Theory
abstract: Recently, a sample meridian estimator of location parameter (LP) has been proposed. It has been shown to be robust and adjustable by means of tunable parameter δ. Basic properties of this estimator were studied; however its practical behavior needs further analysis. In this paper, we study and analyze the efficiency of the meridian estimator for samples with essentially different properties. For this purpose, we use generalized Gaussian distribution as a model. Also, the efficiency of the meridian estimator is compared to the efficiency of median and myriad estimators.

articleTitle: Finite differences variable grid evaluation of TE modes in metallic ridge waveguides
publicationTitle: 2010 International Conference on Mathematical Methods in Electromagnetic Theory
abstract: A new general scheme for the FD approximation of the Laplace operator, based on a non-regular discretization, is discussed here. It allows to take into account in the FD scheme the boundary conditions, and therefore allows to use the exact shape of the boundary. As a consequence, the field distribution details can be more accurately modeled. This approach has been applied to mode evaluation in ridged waveguides, and allows a precise evaluation of the power capability of those guides.

articleTitle: External electromagnetic field of MWNT antennas
publicationTitle: 2010 International Conference on Mathematical Methods in Electromagnetic Theory
abstract: The problem about construction of the external electromagnetic field created by MWNT antennas is considered. For the description of such field Lorentz -Maxwell average microscopic equations are used. Each element of the multilayered antenna is described with the help of the generalized functions concentrated on smooth surfaces. Such approach allows to present behavior of an electromagnetic field by means of one differential equation which factors are the generalized functions. The special method is developed, allowing obtaining the general solution of the differential equations of the given class. In an obvious kind the exact solution representing external electromagnetic field of MWNT antennas is obtained.

articleTitle: Investigation of diffraction of optical range electromagnetic waves on dielectric nanovibrator
publicationTitle: 2010 International Conference on Mathematical Methods in Electromagnetic Theory
abstract: The antenna under investigation is nanocrystal, covered with a metal film. Complex dielectric permeability of metals in an optical range is considered. The decision of a boundary problem was reduced to the solving integrodifferentianal equations concerning intensity of electric field in the vibrator. The method of solving of this equation, which combines Galerkin method and collocation method is developed. Electrodynamic characteristics of antennas-nanocrystals are investigated.

articleTitle: The properties of carbon nanotube-vibrator parallel to the dielectric-dielectric interface
publicationTitle: 2010 International Conference on Mathematical Methods in Electromagnetic Theory
abstract: Quantum-mechanical properties of carbon nanotube in the model are described by means of macroscopic parameter - surface impedance. Solving of the boundary problem for impedance vibrator was reduced to solving of Paired Integral Equations (PIE) in Fourier transformation of current on the vibrator. PIEs were solved by means of Galerkin method with Chebyshev basis. The influence of substrate on amplitude-phase characteristics of the nanotube antenna was investigated.

articleTitle: Linear and nonlinear resonances in Bragg layered structures with lumped parallel reactive inhomogeneities
publicationTitle: 2010 International Conference on Mathematical Methods in Electromagnetic Theory
abstract: Scattering of plane monochromatic waves on quasiperiodic layered structures is considered. Exact solutions for complex amplitudes of reflected and transmitted waves are found by method of transmission matrices. Influence of connection of lumped elements on resonance properties of Bragg resonators is investigated. Optimal values of reactive conductivity for different values of thickness of central layer are found. Shifting of resonance frequency for nonoptimal values of conductivity of shunt element is considered. Hysteresis behavior is observed for case of Kerr nonlinearity.

articleTitle: Eigenvalues and eigenfunctions of plane waveguide with differ walls impedances
publicationTitle: 2010 International Conference on Mathematical Methods in Electromagnetic Theory
abstract: The analytical solution of excitation of the plane waveguide with perfectly conductive walls which coincide with the coordinate plane is well-known. In the case of lossy walls the problem can be reduced to transcendental equation which can be solved numerically. A numerical method and the results of eigenvalues derivation for the case of arbitrary non-zero walls' impedances are presented. The method presented guaranties roots isolation.

articleTitle: Construction and use of reproducing kernels for boundary and eigenvalue problems in the plane using pseudoanalytic function theory
publicationTitle: 2010 International Conference on Mathematical Methods in Electromagnetic Theory
abstract: We show how the Bergman-type reproducing kernels for the elliptic operator D = div pgrad+ q with variable coefficients defined in a bounded domain in the plane can be constructed using pseudoanalytic function theory and in particular pseudoanalytic formal powers. Under certain conditions on the coefficients p and q and with the aid of pseudoanalytic function theory a complete system of null solutions of the operator can be obtained following a simple algorithm consisting in recursive integration. Then the complete system of solutions is used for constructing the corresponding reproducing kernel. We study theoretical and numerical aspects of the method.

articleTitle: Numerical algorythm for the scattering by imperfect strips using the nystrom-type discretization
publicationTitle: 2010 International Conference on Mathematical Methods in Electromagnetic Theory
abstract: The problem of the H-polarized electromagnetic plane wave scattering by a flat thin imperfect (i.e. not perfectly electric conducting but partially transparent or lossy) strip with identical face properties is solved using two decoupled singular integral equations. Attention is concentrated on the construction of the discrete model. The use of the Nystrom-type numerical algorithm, based on the interpolation type quadrature formulas, is numerically efficient and guarantees a fast convergence and controlled accuracy of computations.

articleTitle: Natural modes of weakly guiding optical fiber
publicationTitle: 2010 International Conference on Mathematical Methods in Electromagnetic Theory
abstract: The eigenvalue problem for generalized natural modes of an inhomogeneous optical fiber is formulated as a problem for the Helmholtz equation with Reichardt condition at infinity in the cross-sectional plane. The generalized eigenvalues of this problem are the complex propagation constants on a logarithmic Reimann surface. The original problem is reduced to a spectral problem with compact integral operator. Theorem on spectrum localization is proved, and then it is proved that the set of all eigenvalues of the original problem can only be a set of isolated points on the Reimann surface, and it also proved that each eigenvalue depends continuously on the frequency and can appear and disappear only at the boundary of the Reimann surface. The existence of the surface modes is proved. The Galerkin method for numerical calculation of the surface modes is proposed. Some results of the numerical experiments are presented.

articleTitle: A flange surface impedance influence on radiation efficiency of finite plane waveguide array
publicationTitle: 2010 International Conference on Mathematical Methods in Electromagnetic Theory
abstract: In this paper the radiation pattern of the finite phased array of plane waveguides with an impedance flange has been theoretically investigated. The array radiation has been considered as superposition of radiation of each waveguide. Mutual coupling between waveguide apertures has been taken into account using variational principle in the single-mode approximation. Some numerical results for the array of eleven and fourty waveguides have been presented.

articleTitle: Trapped mode resonances in optical planar periodical structures with metal and dielectric elements
publicationTitle: 2010 International Conference on Mathematical Methods in Electromagnetic Theory
abstract: The problem of infra red light diffraction on a planar 2-D periodic metal-dielectric or dielectric structures with square periodic cell has been solved. The periodic cell includes either two complex-shaped asymmetric metal elements or two dielectric bars with different lengths. The existence of a high order trapped mode resonance was shown for metal-dielectric structure and its properties were studied. For the first time, the existence of a trapped mode resonance in a dielectric planar structure was shown. Such resonances demonstrate greater quality factor then usual plasmon-polariton resonances.

articleTitle: Numerical evaluation of the eigenexpansion of the electrostatic potential near a dielectric cone
publicationTitle: 2010 International Conference on Mathematical Methods in Electromagnetic Theory
abstract: The purpose of this paper is to elaborate on some numerical aspects of the evaluation of the eigenfunction expansion for the electrostatic potential near a dielectric cone of circular cross-section. This expansion has been derived analytically by the authors in a recent article [SIAM J. Appl. Math., 70 (2010), pp. 2329-2352] with the aid of the two-interval Sturm-Liouville theory. In our effort to implement numerically the aforesaid expansion we discovered a numerical instability on the spherical surface which is centered at the vertex of the cone and passes through the point source. In this paper we present an analytical way of removing that instability. Furthermore, we propose some numerical methods for calculating the terms of the eigenfunction expansion and we present some numerical results in the form of equipotential contour plots.

articleTitle: Application of fractional boundary conditions in diffraction by plane screens
publicationTitle: 2010 International Conference on Mathematical Methods in Electromagnetic Theory
abstract: Problems of diffraction by plane screens described by fractional boundary conditions (FBC) are considered. FBC involves fractional derivative of tangential field components. FBC can be treated as intermediate case between well known boundary conditions for perfectly electric conductor (PEC) and perfectly magnetic conductor (PMC). A method to solve two-dimensional problems of scattering of E-polarized plane wave on a strip and half plane with FBC is proposed. The considered problems are reduced to coupled integral equations which are discretized using orthogonal polynomials. The method allows to obtain physical characteristics with any desired accuracy. One important feature of the considered integral equations is noted: these equations can be solved analytically for one special value of the fractional order equal to 0.5 for any frequency.

articleTitle: Scattering of electromagnetic pulse on the impedance strip into the dielectric layer
publicationTitle: 2010 International Conference on Mathematical Methods in Electromagnetic Theory
abstract: Paper examines the problem of diffraction the short electromagnetic pulse on the impedance strip. Strip is located into the thickness dielectric layer, which is been located between two dielectric half-spaces. Are obtained the integral equations of the problem, which then are reduced to the infinite system of linear algebraic equations. The influence of the geometric parameters of structure on the angular distributions of scattering field is examined.

articleTitle: Synthesis of antennas with specific pattern and polarization properties based on complex materials
publicationTitle: 2010 International Conference on Mathematical Methods in Electromagnetic Theory
abstract: In this paper is considered the synthesis of antennas with flat pattern in certain angle which has circular polarization of radiation. This antenna is based on complex materials and represents the dielectric body in which the resonance admixture elements lattice is embedded. Here is considered numerical simulation of this problem using the Method of Auxiliary Sources (MAS).

articleTitle: Resonant antenna based on CRLH TL
publicationTitle: 2010 International Conference on Mathematical Methods in Electromagnetic Theory
abstract: In this paper, a study of the compact microstrip antenna based on composite right/left handed (CRLH) metamaterial transmission line is presented. The physical size and operational frequencies of the antenna are determined by the CRLH metamaterial's unit cell. The antenna exhibits monopolar radiation at its fundamental mode of resonant frequency. As it is well known that the composite right/left-handed (CRLH) transmission line (TL) has unique property of an infinite-wavelength wave at specific non-zero frequency because of zero permittivity and permeability. Generally, CRLH includes both LH series C/shunt L and parasitic RH series L/shunt C in its circuit model, resulting in a structure which is LH at lower frequencies and RH at higher frequencies. The operation bandwidth cover the required band widths of the IEEE 802.11 wireless local-area networks (WLAN) standards and worldwide interoperability for microwave access (WiMax) in the 2.97 GHz, 3.345GHz and 3.79 GHz (3.49-3.79 GHz). The zeroth order resonant frequency was found to be at 3.79GHz.

articleTitle: Polarization transformation of electromagnetic waves on a reflector array of the short-circuited coaxial-sector waveguides
publicationTitle: 2010 International Conference on Mathematical Methods in Electromagnetic Theory
abstract: Polarization characteristics reflective two-dimensionally periodic array from the short-circuited coaxial-sector waveguides are investigated. Frequency dependencies of Stokes parameters of the reflected wave are presented at normal and oblique incidence on an array of the plane linearly polarised electromagnetic wave. Dependencies of Stokes parameters on length of the short-circuited coaxial-sector waveguides are calculated.

articleTitle: Investigation of tangential wave propagation under a stratified anisotropic structure
publicationTitle: 2010 International Conference on Mathematical Methods in Electromagnetic Theory
abstract: It is investigated a wave propagating along a stratified anisotropic structure. A dependence of the reflection coefficient on an orientation of the anisotropy axis is studied. The so-call “penetration effect” is described mathematically for the case of tangential wave propagation under a structure. It is offered to use the obtained results for creating an analog frequency demodulator in the terahertz domain.

articleTitle: Near-field behavior in the method of auxiliary sources (MAS) for a simple scattering problem
publicationTitle: 2010 International Conference on Mathematical Methods in Electromagnetic Theory
abstract: It has been recently observed that, when one applies the Method of Auxiliary Sources (MAS) to scattering problems involving an infinite circular cylinder illuminated by an electric current filament, it is possible to have divergent auxiliary currents together with a convergent field. In this paper, we investigate the near-field behavior for the so-called “cylindrical problem” with discrete auxiliary sources, in the region within the critical distance, where the aforementioned divergence appears as abnormal, rapid oscillations. We provide numerical results and derive an asymptotic formula for the case of a large number of sources that reveals the properties of the near field.

articleTitle: Calculation of tem-modes in the waveguides having orthogon cross-section
publicationTitle: 2010 International Conference on Mathematical Methods in Electromagnetic Theory
abstract: A general analysis for the modal characterization of multiply connected, hollow, conducting waveguides is presented. It is relevant to waveguides with an orthogon cross-section. The transverse electromagnetic (TEM)-modes are analyzed. The approach described allows getting the exact and high-speed algorithm which lends itself naturally to parallelization.

articleTitle: Non-parametric detection scheme for isotropic image texture with normal increments
publicationTitle: 2010 International Conference on Mathematical Methods in Electromagnetic Theory
abstract: We analyze applicability of 2D fractal Brownian motion (fBm) for real-life image textures with respect to two general fBm properties: isotropy and normality of its increments. A non-parametric detection scheme for texture satisfying these two properties is proposed. It is based on Lilliefors test for texture increments normality and Kolmogorov-Smirnov two samples test for equality of distributions of pairs of increments. The scheme is tested against large real-life images database and is shown to detect and remove such image patterns as edges, areas with clipping effects, irregular and anisotropic textures.

articleTitle: Radar cross-section calculation method for antenna of P-18 radar station
publicationTitle: 2010 International Conference on Mathematical Methods in Electromagnetic Theory
abstract: The scattered electromagnetic field calculation method for finite cylinder with resonant cross-section is considered. The method is used for calculation of radar cross-section for antenna of P-18 radar station. Also radar cross-sections for perfectly conducting antenna and antenna partially made of perfectly absorbing materials (Macdonald model) are compared.

articleTitle: Improved kernels for method-of-moments analyses of resonant circular arrays of cylindrical dipoles
publicationTitle: 2010 International Conference on Mathematical Methods in Electromagnetic Theory
abstract: We perform a Method-of-Moments (MoM) analysis of a circular array of cylindrical dipoles. Such arrays are known from earlier theoretical and experimental studies to possess very narrow resonances. The earlier studies were carried out using the “two-term theory.” The present work is a direct continuation of a recent paper showing that the problem possesses unique and particular difficulties. The main difficulties are overcome herein using a set of improved kernels in the usual Halliin-type integral equations (these kernels had been developed in previous works, and were successfully incorporated into the aforementioned two-term theory analyses). We make a comparison of our MoM results to two-term theory results for the case of a 20-element array.

articleTitle: EM wave diffraction by semi-infinite strip grating
publicationTitle: 2010 International Conference on Mathematical Methods in Electromagnetic Theory
abstract: The operator method solving the diffraction by a semi-infinite grating (SIG) of plane metal strips is suggested in this paper. A point of peculiar interest in this method is the application of specific translation symmetry of the structure that means that no SIG properties change with its last element removed. This results in a nonlinear operator equation with respect to the unknown integral SIG scattering operator. The equation is approximately solved by the developed numerical technique, and the calculated characteristics of the SIG-reflected field in the region above the structure are analyzed for different numerical values of the exciting wave angle of incidence, the strip width and the incident field wavelength.

articleTitle: Em wave scattering by perfectly conducting disk of finite thickness
publicationTitle: 2010 International Conference on Mathematical Methods in Electromagnetic Theory
abstract: Calculation technique for modeling of scattering characteristics for perfectly electrically conducting (PEC) disk of finite thickness is proposed. Employed algorithms are based on solving surface integral equations (IE) of the 1<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">st</sup> and 2<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">nd</sup> kind. The results of radar cross section (RCS) calculation for discs with various thicknesses are compared with exact results for infinitely thin disc. The backscattered radiation patterns of thin disc in E- and H-planes are presented.

articleTitle: Interaction of counterpropagating electromagnetic waves in the absorbing plate, placed in a waveguide
publicationTitle: 2010 International Conference on Mathematical Methods in Electromagnetic Theory
abstract: Interaction of two counterpropagating coherent transverse-electric electromagnetic waves in the absorbing plate, placed in a waveguide of arbitrary cross section, is considered. It is supposed, that the waves with various initial phases incident on the boundaries of the plate from two sides. The analytical expression for the power transmission interference coefficient is found. Some physical features of tunnel interference in a plate are revealed.

articleTitle: Application of integral equations to the simulation of diffraction grating based on chirped mirror
publicationTitle: 2010 International Conference on Mathematical Methods in Electromagnetic Theory
abstract: A method of integral equations (IE) is applied to a simulation of diffraction efficiency (DE) of metal-dielectric and all-dielectric diffraction gratings (DG). Two factors narrowing the spectral band of laser pulse reflection into minus first space harmonics (MFSH) are analyzed. It is found that by using a chirped mirror instead of a multilayer all-dielectric one for non-Littrow mounted DG it is possible to achieve the DE over 95% in 90 nm wide spectral window.

articleTitle: Electromagnetic field evolution in a linear chain of coupled resonators with time discontinuity in permittivity
publicationTitle: 2010 International Conference on Mathematical Methods in Electromagnetic Theory
abstract: The paper presents a theoretical analysis of the electromagnetic field evolution in a linear chain of coupled circular dielectric resonators when their material is subject to abrupt time change in permittivity. Possibilities of the frequency shift are discussed.

articleTitle: About possibilities of scanning the beam from a set of transverse slots in rectangular waveguide with dielectric layer
publicationTitle: 2010 International Conference on Mathematical Methods in Electromagnetic Theory
abstract: The properties of a frequency scanning antenna on the base of slotted waveguide used as slowing down system are studied. The waveguide is rectangular, slots in the broad wall are transverse, the dielectric layer is parallel to the waveguide broad walls.

articleTitle: Electrodynamics analysis of multilayer multislot and multistrip periodical structures
publicationTitle: 2010 International Conference on Mathematical Methods in Electromagnetic Theory
abstract: The numerical-analytical approach was developed for analysis of various multi-layer, multi-strip and multi-slot periodical planar structures. Shown, that approach has high accuracy and requires small computer resources.

articleTitle: Computer based algorithm to design metamaterials
publicationTitle: 2010 International Conference on Mathematical Methods in Electromagnetic Theory
abstract: In this paper, a computer based algorithm is developed for designing conventional split ring and thin wire based metamaterials with negative refractive index. The effects of the variation of the geometrical parameters on the effective permittivity and permeability of the designed structures are observed numerically to form optimum composite structures. At the end, one optimum design is given using the mentioned home-developed computer algorithm and it is shown that the refraction index of the designed metamaterial structure has a pronounced bandwidth where the permittivity and permeability are simultaneously negative.

articleTitle: Electromagnetic wave scattering by periodically structured chains of closely spaced sub-wavelength wires
publicationTitle: 2010 International Conference on Mathematical Methods in Electromagnetic Theory
abstract: Using the field expansions in local coordinates and addition theorems for cylindrical functions, we consider the problem of the H-polarized waves scattered by finite chains of circular wires. The scattering and absorption cross-sections are found numerically and localized-plasmon and periodicity-caused resonances are studied for the visible light scattering by the grids of closely spaced nanowires made of silver.

articleTitle: Modeling pulse radiation of rod antenna by method of mode matching in time domain
publicationTitle: 2010 International Conference on Mathematical Methods in Electromagnetic Theory
abstract: The paper considers using the method of mode matching in time domain for simulation of a pulse signal propagation in a dielectric circular rod antenna. The mode basis for circular dielectric waveguide and free space are obtained. The systems of integral-differential evolutionary equations for dielectric waveguide and free space are reduced to the system of matrix differential equations by the method of moments. Numerical solution scheme for these systems by FDTD method are proposed. In order to calculate signal radiation by the rod antenna the field matching procedure based on the boundary conditions is proposed.

articleTitle: Numerical modeling and design of EBG waveguides and componets
publicationTitle: 2010 International Conference on Mathematical Methods in Electromagnetic Theory
abstract: Novel waveguide circuits for microwave and millimeter wave applications based on electromagnetic bandgap (EBG) structures are presented. The following aspects of the problem are discussed: fundamentals of compensating sources technique (CST) for EBG circuits design, numerical analysis of regular waveguides inside EBG arrays, analysis and experimental investigation of EBG components.

articleTitle: Numerical modeling and design of EBG devices and antennas
publicationTitle: 2010 International Conference on Mathematical Methods in Electromagnetic Theory
abstract: Novel waveguide devices and antennas for microwave and millimeter wave applications based on electromagnetic bandgap (EBG) structures are presented. The following aspects of the problem are discussed: numerical analysis of elementary and complex EBG power dividers and antenna arrays on their base and analysis of systems of coupled EBG waveguides and design of beam-forming networks (BFN).

articleTitle: Electromagnetic theory of sound and phonons in liquid
publicationTitle: 2010 International Conference on Mathematical Methods in Electromagnetic Theory
abstract: Sound waves in dielectric liquid, that consists of subsystems of valence electrons with effective mass and ions which interact through the long-wave potential electric field are considered, on analogies with metallic liquid, but with a requirement, that electric current is absent. It is shown that usual description of sound wave in an ideal liquid as wave of mass density and mass velocity follows from the offered consideration. It is also shown that sound waves on the other hand can be considered as waves of potential electric field in an environment. Introduction of phonons in both cases is considered.

articleTitle: Asymptotic solution of EM field wave scattering problem by small bodies: Single body case
publicationTitle: 2010 International Conference on Mathematical Methods in Electromagnetic Theory
abstract: The problem of electromagnetic wave scattering by many small bodies is reduced to solving a Fredholm second-kind integral equation. This equation is solved asymptotically as the characteristic size a of the small bodies tends to zero. The numerical solution of this Fredholm equation is compared with asymptotic solution. Numerical results are presented in the case of single body. The difference between the numerical and asymptotic solutions tends to zero when a → 0.

articleTitle: Variation of large particle size for gas discharge particles-in-cells simulation
publicationTitle: 2010 International Conference on Mathematical Methods in Electromagnetic Theory
abstract: Large particle size variation method was developed and tested for the computer simulation of pulse gas discharge inside dielectric cell via large particles-in-cells (PIC) method. Simulations were carried out with and without large particles' size variation. Comparison between these simulations' results was held for discharge current waveforms, particles' numbers, spatial locations and velocity distributions. Results agrees with each other qualitatively and, in most cases, quantitatively. The main flaw of the large particles' variation method is additional digital noise.

articleTitle: Numerical algorithm for modeling the processes of establishing a normal regime of glow discharge in 2D geometry
publicationTitle: 2010 International Conference on Mathematical Methods in Electromagnetic Theory
abstract: 2D hydrodynamic computer simulation of non stationary regimes of the glow discharge was developed. The collision ionization, electron-ions recombination and secondary electron emission were taken into account in the model. Model allows carrying out calculations of non-stationary regimes of the glow discharge.

articleTitle: Wave scattering by nonlinear semiconductor layers
publicationTitle: 2010 International Conference on Mathematical Methods in Electromagnetic Theory
abstract: The combinatorial frequency generation by the semiconductor layer illuminated by the plane waves of two tones is investigated. The nonlinearity is due to the nonlinear free-carrier current in the semiconductor. The three-wave interaction technique is applied to study the nonlinear processes. The effect of the physical and geometrical parameters of the layers on the reflected and transmitted waves' intensities of combinatorial frequencies is examined.

articleTitle: Propagation of TM wave in a layer with Kerr law nonlinearity
publicationTitle: 2010 International Conference on Mathematical Methods in Electromagnetic Theory
abstract: Propagation of TM electromagnetic waves through a nonlinear homogeneous nonmagnetic isotropic dielectric layer is considered. The layer is located between two homogeneous isotropic half-spaces with constant permittivities. The permittivity in the layer obeys the Kerr law. The dispersion equation for the propagation constants of the waves in the layer is presented. Presented results allow to study nonlinear material and nonlinear metamaterial.

articleTitle: Resonance field analysis and electromagnetic coupling effects in metamaterial structures
publicationTitle: 2010 International Conference on Mathematical Methods in Electromagnetic Theory
abstract: The results of full-wave simulations of resonance responses of metamaterial structures incorporating multiple unit cells are presented. The structures under consideration include conventional metamaterials comprising arrays of split-ring resonators and cut wires, metamaterials composed of dielectric resonators, and electromagnetic shell-type cloaks consisting of either metallic or dielectric resonator arrays. The conducted studies have revealed drastic interactions between partcles in all types of metamaterials that can modify the mechanisms of wave propagation in these structures and need to be accounted for at the designing of metamaterials. The potential of utilizing integrated resonance responses to increase the tailorability of metamaterial properties is demonstrated.

articleTitle: Wave polarization at RF radiation sources direction estimation by regularization and nonlinear pseudoinversion methods
publicationTitle: 2010 International Conference on Mathematical Methods in Electromagnetic Theory
abstract: A problem of polarization independent spatial tracking of coherent signal sources energy is investigated within a nonlinear regularization theory framework based on l<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">p</inf> norm. The efficiency of proposed algorithms for digital reconstruction of energy angular distribution for intricately polarized multibeam electromagnetic field is confirmed by numerical simulation of circular antenna array.

articleTitle: Numerical investigation of screening properties of thin composite shells
publicationTitle: 2010 International Conference on Mathematical Methods in Electromagnetic Theory
abstract: The boundary problem of penetrating the monochromatic electromagnetic field which represents the arbitrary combination of E- and H-polarized plane fields, through a thin cylindrical shell made of biisotropic material with arbitrary complex parameters of media has been solved. The solution of the problem has amounted to solving a system of integral equations by means of specialized two-sided boundary conditions on the composite shell surface. The system of integral equations has been numerically solved by a quadrature method.

articleTitle: Advances on circuit modeling of extraordinary transmission
publicationTitle: 2010 International Conference on Mathematical Methods in Electromagnetic Theory
abstract: Extraordinary optical transmission (EOT) is a phenomenon which has received extraordinary attention since its discovery, twelve years ago. The phenomenon takes place at any frequency range - not only at the optical regime -, and it has been explained in terms of the excitation of surface waves along the periodically structured metal screens used in the experiments. EOT also takes place, however, through slit gratings for a polarization precluding the excitation of such surface waves. It can be also observed through electrically small diaphragms located inside hollow pipe waveguides. Along the last three years, some of the authors have developed models explaining the phenomenon in terms of simple concepts extracted from conventional waveguide theory. The models lead themselves to simple circuit equivalents which help the understanding of the underlying physics. This paper summarizes the main results obtained by the members of the group and some other collaborators concerning the capabilities of the proposed approach.

articleTitle: The second lorentz theorem and operator form of the power conservation law
publicationTitle: 2010 International Conference on Mathematical Methods in Electromagnetic Theory
abstract: The function of the second Lorentz theorem in deriving the operator form of the generalized power conservation law is considered. Some new forms of this law for the mode-diffraction problem are found. The revealed fundamental properties of the scattering operator matrices are analyzed. The presented results can be useful for application in analytic-numerical methods based on the modal analysis.

articleTitle: New exact solutions for cylindrical axisymmetric waves in a nonlinear nondispersive medium
publicationTitle: 2010 International Conference on Mathematical Methods in Electromagnetic Theory
abstract: We present a new method for deriving exact solutions of the Maxwell equations in a nonlinear medium without dispersion. It is assumed that the medium considered lacks a center of inversion and the dependence of the electric displacement on the electric field can be approximated by an exponential function. Using this method, a solution is obtained that describes the propagation of cylindrical electromagnetic waves in such a medium.

articleTitle: Bilateral approach for the dispersion characteristic of waves over the open comb
publicationTitle: 2010 International Conference on Mathematical Methods in Electromagnetic Theory
abstract: Closure equation, witch takes into account both the dispersion and amplitude properties in both regions of open comb, was obtained. On the basis of the closure equation the bilateral approximations were theoretically justified for the eigen waves of open comb. Regularities for the numbers of accountable space harmonics, using the system of certain order for oscillations in resonators, were found for bilateral approximations to obtain the lowest average error. Bilateral approximations are correct for the comb with the combs of finite thickness. Accuracy of calculation has an order of magnitude higher, than the one with the same order has without bilateral approximations.

articleTitle: Electromagnetic field state description with correlation functions of different nature
publicationTitle: 2010 International Conference on Mathematical Methods in Electromagnetic Theory
abstract: Modern electromagnetic theory based on quantum conceptions supposes turn to averages of operator dynamic variables for describing the field state and analyzing experimental results with computational methods. Theoretical analysis of such non-equilibrium phenomenon as Dicke superfluorescence leads to an algebra of variables which are necessary for building a set of evolution equations. Rather different correlation functions can be determined in measurements according to the coincidence scheme using Glauber's quantum detectors. A natural way of connecting various correlation functions is expressing them via the photon density matrix and Wigner function. The problem of comparing the theoretical and experimental approaches is analyzed in the present paper.

articleTitle: Electromagnetic field ellipticity in the case of reflection from fine-stratified structure located on a metal substrate
publicationTitle: 2010 International Conference on Mathematical Methods in Electromagnetic Theory
abstract: Reflection of a plane electromagnetic wave from the fine-stratified structure located on a metal substrate is considered. A number of features caused by specific properties of effective permittivity are arises. It has been shown, that dependences on a frequency and magnetic field allow to change polarizing characteristics (field ellipticity).

articleTitle: Wave beam dispersion on semiinfinite rectangular waveguides phased-array antenna
publicationTitle: 2010 International Conference on Mathematical Methods in Electromagnetic Theory
abstract: Linearly polarized three-dimensional Gaussian wave beam dispersion on semi-infinite rectangular cross section waveguides phased-array antenna problem has been solved by operator method. Far-field pattern of reflected electromagnetic field has been calculated.

articleTitle: Calculation of electric field lines of eigen waves of an open comb
publicationTitle: 2010 International Conference on Mathematical Methods in Electromagnetic Theory
abstract: Based on the numerical solution of the boundary problem is designed and built electric field lines of eigen waves of an open comb. The distribution of an electric field in the open comb is not as simple as usually portrayed.

articleTitle: Three-dimensional Gaussian beam scattering from an anisotropic slab
publicationTitle: 2010 International Conference on Mathematical Methods in Electromagnetic Theory
abstract: The problem of the scattering of 3-D Gaussian beam incident at an arbitrary angle onto a double-periodic magneto-dielectric slab has been formulated and solved. The new formulas for incident and scattered 3-D Gaussian beam fields in the form of the single integrals have been derived. They allow to reduce the time spent upon the numerical calculations of the incident and scattered beam fields.

articleTitle: Features of the gyrotropic wave propagation in the homogeneous ionosphere
publicationTitle: 2010 International Conference on Mathematical Methods in Electromagnetic Theory
abstract: The quasi-stationary Maxwell equations of the gyrotropic waves have been examined. In contrast to the approach used in the other papers [1]-[3] the general form of the electromagnetic equation of the gyrotropic waves has been considered. The dispersion equation analysis shows that attenuation of one of the mode tends to zero in the perpendicular to the magnetic field direction while along this direction the attenuation is finite (Fig. 1). Basing on this feature we can suppose that low frequency electromagnetic fluctuations tend to expand along the magnetic field. It forms in the ionosphere long areas with invariable direction of the electric field and current and weakly variable magnitude of these parameters. To check this conclusion the direct problem of the evolution of an electromagnetic fluctuation has been solved numerically. The results show that spherically symmetric fluctuation expands along the magnetic field lines by 5-30 times while in some cases the widening is fully absent (Fig. 2).

articleTitle: Numerical study of electromagnetic field scattering by an electrically resistive disk
publicationTitle: 2010 International Conference on Mathematical Methods in Electromagnetic Theory
abstract: In this paper, we study the scattering problem of a given time-harmonic electromagnetic wave by a thin electrically resistive disk. We consider a horizontal ring of electric current as a source of the incident field. To find the solution of the problem, we use analytical-numerical scheme which is based on the generalized boundary conditions, dual integral equations, and the method of analytical regularization. We present the normalized radiation patterns and total radiated power for different values of geometrical and material parameters.

articleTitle: Diffraction of electromagnetic wave on finite carbon nanotube array perpendicular to interface of mediums
publicationTitle: 2010 International Conference on Mathematical Methods in Electromagnetic Theory
abstract: In preset work boundary problem of electromagnetic wave diffraction on array of carbon nanotubes - dipoles (CNT) is reduced to system of integro-differential equations (IDE). To avoid difficulties concerned with singularity as well as to reduce computation time kernels of these IDEs are presented in form of Fourier integral. The IDEs are solved by Galerkin's method with Chebyshev basis. Influence of substrate on amplitude-frequency characteristics and radiation pattern of CNT are investigated. It is found while distance between CNTs decreases resonant frequency and magnitude of scattered field are increases.

articleTitle: Estimation and analisys of thermal response of human tissue during EM exposure
publicationTitle: 2010 International Conference on Mathematical Methods in Electromagnetic Theory
abstract: During last decades, the environment has undergone serious changes from EM point of view. The objective of this paper is to analyze realistic exposure scenarios by means of numerical computations. Our aim is to determine peak values of SAR and temperature rise for various frequencies and antenna lengths. This paper contains results of computer simulations performed on a human model.

articleTitle: Electromagnetic waves diffraction on a system of open cones in time domain
publicationTitle: 2010 International Conference on Mathematical Methods in Electromagnetic Theory
abstract: A model problem of electromagnetic waves diffraction on an equalperiodical multilayered perfectly conducting conical grating is considered. The solution method is based on using the Meler-Fock integral transforms and the method of the coupling problem. This allows both analytical and numerical solutions obtaining. The graphs representing the electric field component dependencies on the time parameter are provided for the case of the single cone with a longitudinal slot.

articleTitle: Effect of the off-focus shift of the feed on the radiation characteristics of a 2-D parabolic reflector antenna
publicationTitle: 2010 International Conference on Mathematical Methods in Electromagnetic Theory
abstract: The parabolic reflector antennas are widely used in the telecommunication systems and generally have large aperture sizes like 50λ to 80λ and larger. Their reliable full-wave analysis with the conventional Method of Moments (MoM) or with the other numerical methods is difficult because of inaccessible speed and accuracy. This statement is valid both for 3D and 2D reflector antennas in both polarizations. The Method of Analytical Regularization (MAR) constitutes an alternative solution compared to the ordinary MoM, which can provide only 1–2 digit accuracy. It provides finer accuracy within a reasonable computation time because the computational error can be decreased simply by increasing the matrix size in MAR. We have previously developed this method for the accurate simulation of the arbitrary conical section profile 2D reflector antennas, and the corresponding codes have provided us with accurate benchmark data. Here we study a similar problem however with the feed simulated by Complex Source Point (CSP) source located at an off-focus point on the symmetry axis of a front-fed reflector antenna. The numerical results are presented for the radiation characteristics including the forward and backward directivities and the radiation patterns in all directions.

articleTitle: Electromagnetic theory of sound in metal
publicationTitle: 2010 International Conference on Mathematical Methods in Electromagnetic Theory
abstract: The theory of sound in an isotropic solid neglecting by dissipation in the adiabatic approximation taking into account internal electromagnetic field is built. The resiliency of solid is modeled by pressure of Fermi-gas of electrons and by the effective external magnetic field with equal to zero first and different from zero second correlation moment. It is shown that sound waves it is possible to consider equivalently as waves of the electromagnetic field in solid, and as waves of displacement vector. Expressions for transversal and longitudinal velocities of sound through introduced effective parameters are received.

articleTitle: Analysis of local Drude-Born-Fedorov constitutive relations for time-dependent waves in chiral media
publicationTitle: 2010 International Conference on Mathematical Methods in Electromagnetic Theory
abstract: The Maxwell system for time-dependent electromagnetic fields in a chiral medium is considered. Its equivalent form as a single biquaternionic equation is used for obtaining a general solution in the one-dimensional case. Analysis of the solution leads to conclusions about possible configurations of the field. The dependence of its behavior on the chirality measure is studied.

articleTitle: External magnteic field influence on the transmission properties of the ferrite-dilectric periodic structure bounded by the semiconductor layer
publicationTitle: 2010 International Conference on Mathematical Methods in Electromagnetic Theory
abstract: Transmission properties of the periodic ferrite-dielectric structure interfaced with the semiconductor layer placed into the external magnetic field are investigated in the paper. We analyze cases of TM- and TE- polarized waves. Possibility of control of peaks location in transmission spectrum by changing magnitude of the external magnetic field was demonstrated.

articleTitle: 2.5D Relativistic Electromagnetic PIC code for simulation of beam interaction with plasma in axial-symmetric geometry
publicationTitle: 2010 International Conference on Mathematical Methods in Electromagnetic Theory
abstract: 2.5D relativistic electromagnetic PIC code for simulation of beam interaction with plasma in axial-symmetric geometry was developed. Accurate charge weighting scheme and difference schemes near the system axis were introduced. Simulation tests of electromagnetic wave interaction with inhomogeneous plasma were carried out.

articleTitle: Diffraction by a curved arbitrary screen of finite thickness
publicationTitle: 2010 International Conference on Mathematical Methods in Electromagnetic Theory
abstract: We propose a method for numerical solution of electromagnetic scattering by curved screens of finite thickness, based on solving the integral equation of electric field. The numerical results presented concern the scattering by a spherical screen and a screen, which is not a surface of revolution. Characteristics of scattering by a spherical screen are compared with experimental data.

articleTitle: Long wave layer-specific representation of metamaterial slabs in the microwave frequency range
publicationTitle: 2010 International Conference on Mathematical Methods in Electromagnetic Theory
abstract: In our study, we present a metamaterial slab as a set of infinitely long elementary layers with cross dimension equals the dimension of unit cell of the metamaterial slab. Analytical and numerical optimization method for evaluating the complex effective dielectric and magnetic constants of the elementary layer of the metamaterial by means of solving of the appropriate optimization problem for the metamaterial slab under consideration is presented using the previously obtained long wave approximations of the complex effective constants for the slab considered as a bulk dielectric slab.

articleTitle: Lattice approach to the dynamics of the DPSK-encoded soliton trains
publicationTitle: 2010 International Conference on Mathematical Methods in Electromagnetic Theory
abstract: We study the dynamical properties of the RZ-DPSK encoded sequences, focusing on the instabilities in the soliton train leading to the distortions of the information transmitted. The problem is reformulated within the framework of complex Toda chain model which allows one to carry out the simplified description of the optical soliton dynamics. We elucidate how the bit composition of the pattern affects the initial (linear) stage of the train dynamics and explain the general mechanisms of the appearance of unstable collective soliton modes. Then we discuss the nonlinear regime using asymptotic properties of the pulse stream at large propagation distances and analyze the dynamical behavior of the train classifying different scenarios for the pattern instabilities. Both approaches are based on the machinery of Hermitian and non-Hermitian lattice analysis.

articleTitle: The role of the analytic continuation singularities in the null field method
publicationTitle: 2010 International Conference on Mathematical Methods in Electromagnetic Theory
abstract: The role of the diffraction field analytic continuation singularities in the correct implementation of the null field method is discussed. Theoretical statements are illustrated by numerical calculations.

articleTitle: Integral equation method for modeling the linear electromagnetic response of superconducting films in the mixed state
publicationTitle: 2010 International Conference on Mathematical Methods in Electromagnetic Theory
abstract: A mathematical model describing the linear rf response of thin superconducting films in the mixed state with arbitrary spatial distribution of the vortices and the exciting rf field is developed. The model is formulated in terms of an integro-differential equation, algorithm of numerical solution to which is proposed. The stability of the solution, its dependence on the model parameters and profiles of the magnetic field for symmetric and antisymmetric excitation of rf current inside the film is discussed.

articleTitle: Schwinger-Lippman volume integral equation method for green's function evaluation in an inhomogeneous sphere by an inner source using dini's series expansion
publicationTitle: 2010 International Conference on Mathematical Methods in Electromagnetic Theory
abstract: The fields induced in the interior of penetrable bodies with inhomogeneous compressibility by sources placed inside them are evaluated through a Schwinger-Lippman volume integral equation. In the case of an inhomogeneous sphere, the radial part of the unknown Green's function can be expanded in a double Dini's series, which allows analytical evaluation of the involved cumbersome integrals. The case treated here can be extended to more difficult situations, involving inhomogeneous density, as well as to the corresponding electromagnetic problem, to the elastic problem or even to the electromagnetic problem for cylindrical configuration. Finally, numerical results are given for various inhomogeneous compressibility distributions.

articleTitle: Calculation of radome-enclosed aperture antenna in 3-D
publicationTitle: 2010 International Conference on Mathematical Methods in Electromagnetic Theory
abstract: The exact mathematical model of an aperture antenna and the image theory are used to develop exact and PO integral representations of the fields radiated by radome-enclosed aperture antenna. The desired problem is reduced to finding fields of a plane wave diffracted on the "symmetrized" radome. The passage of the wave through the wall of the radome is analysed by means of geometrical optics. Caustic influence is taken into account, and the contribution of stationary phase points of reflected field to the far-side radiation is discussed. Radiation patterns for antennas with a specified ampliphase distribution enclosed in spherical and parabolic radomes are analysed.

articleTitle: Role of boundary in electomagnetic transients caused by medium time-varyation
publicationTitle: 2010 International Conference on Mathematical Methods in Electromagnetic Theory
abstract: Electromagnetic transients due to presence of boundaries of time-varying medium are investigated. A half-restricted plasma with a plane boundary and a completely restricted plasma in a cylinder and in a sphere are considered. It is shown that interaction of an electromagnetic wave with the time varying plasma changes drastically in the presence of the boundaries compared to the unbounded time varying plasma.

articleTitle: Discrete-ring vortex solitons
publicationTitle: 2010 International Conference on Mathematical Methods in Electromagnetic Theory
abstract: We study analytically and numerically the existence and stability of discrete vortex solitons in the circular arrays of nonlinear optical waveguides, governed by the discrete nonlinear Schrödinger equation. Stable vortex breathers with periodically oscillating topological charge are identified and a continuous interpolating map is constructed which allows to recover trajectories of individual phase dislocations in the form of hyperbolic avoided crossings.

articleTitle: Theoretical and experimental investigation of transition radiation excited by electron bunches in microwaves
publicationTitle: 2010 International Conference on Mathematical Methods in Electromagnetic Theory
abstract: Theoretical and experimental investigation of transition radiation excited by electron bunches crossing the wire screen have been presented. Calculation of transition radiation pattern and estimation of radiation power depending on electron beam modulation have been done. Experimental detection of EM field distribution is in good agreement with the calculation results. The results of calculation of paired grating for electron beam modulation have been shown.

articleTitle: Angle selective properties of one-dimenstion anisotropic photonic crystals
publicationTitle: 2010 International Conference on Mathematical Methods in Electromagnetic Theory
abstract: In the work it is considered an anisotropic photonic crystal with an arbitrary direction of an anisotropy axis. It is studied the dependence of the reflection coefficients on an incidence angle of a plane harmonic wave on a plane-parallel slab. It is found the resonant characteristics in the incidence angle plane. It is offered to use these as a forming of a pattern of optical radiators.

articleTitle: Estimation of rough surface influence on the low-frequency electromagnetic response from the highly conductive object immersed in magnetic soil
publicationTitle: 2010 International Conference on Mathematical Methods in Electromagnetic Theory
abstract: In this paper we present statistical researches, how influences the surfaces roughness of the magnetically susceptible soil on low-frequency magnetic response from the electrically highly-conducting underground object. Data, used for statistical investigation, are obtained by means of numerical simulation. Electromagnetic problem is solved using method of auxiliary sources for the electrically highly-conducting object placed in magnetically susceptible soil with rough surface. GEM3 sensor is modeled as excitant in the electromagnetic problem. Different models of rough surfaces with axial-symmetry are considered. Surfaces models are constructed based on piecewise defined by polynomials fifth order spline, which interpolates set of equidistant radial points with random heights. The probability density function of low-frequency magnetic response is built a priori based on results related to different cases of surface roughness.

articleTitle: [Copyright notice]
publicationTitle: 2010 International Conference on Mathematical Methods in Electromagnetic Theory
abstract: The following topics are dealt with: optics; photonics; geoscience; remote sensing; waveguide circuits; time-domain electromagnetics; antennas; computational techniques; nano electromagnetics; micro electromagnetics; nonclassical electromagnetics; analytical regularization; electromagnetic theory; bandgap; metamaterials; integral equation techniques; scattering; diffraction; inverse problem; and nonlinear problem.
